headline: Latent haplotypes, linkage structure and unsampled phylogeny regions made explicit
label: Explicit Latent Structure Inference
summary: Preprints now treat haplotypes, linkage disequilibrium and unsampled phylogeny regions as explicit latent targets.
synthesis: The common thread in this set is replacing a simplifying step with an explicit formulation of an unobserved quantity. DiGi treats diploid genotyping on a pangenome haplotype trellis graph as an exact integer program, jointly inferring two haplotype paths from reads. LDEN estimates whole-genome linkage disequilibrium from short-read viral sequencing data by alternating projections onto positive semidefinite matrices, so the target is fitted under explicit constraints. The third item applies machine learning and beam search to localize unsampled regions in partially sampled pathogen phylogenies from the observed tree alone; its connection to the first two is weaker. What is new is the target itself: haplotype configurations, genome-wide linkage structure and unsampled phylogenetic portions are each modeled as latent objects to be inferred.
